recipes.title: Salt Licorice Protein Ice Cream
recipes.summary: Black, salty and faintly medicinal in the best Nordic way, with enough protein to pass as breakfast.
recipes.imageAlt: A dark, near-black scoop of salt licorice ice cream in a bowl
recipes.article: Licorice is a flavour that punishes half measures. Go light on it and you get a grey pint that tastes vaguely of aniseed; commit, and you get something genuinely worth making. This one commits. Licorice powder does the heavy lifting, salmiak sharpens it into proper salty licorice, and the mascarpone keeps the whole thing from turning chalky the way protein bases often do. The xanthan gum is not optional if you want a smooth first spin. Protein powder holds very little fat, and fat is what normally stops ice crystals forming, so the gum stands in for it. A quarter teaspoon is enough to change the texture completely, and a whole teaspoon would make it slimy.

steps.title: Whisk the dry mix
steps.detail: Whisk all the dry ingredients together in a bowl for a good thirty seconds, until the colour is even and no pale streaks of protein powder remain.

steps.title: Blend the base
steps.detail: Add the dry mix and all the wet ingredients to a blender and run until completely smooth, about 45 seconds. Stop once to scrape the sides.

steps.title: Fill the pint
steps.detail: Pour into the pint container, stopping at the MAX FILL line.

steps.title: Freeze level
steps.detail: Level the surface with a spoon, fit the lid, and freeze flat for a full 24 hours.

steps.title: Spin
steps.detail: Spin on LITE ICE CREAM straight from the freezer.

steps.title: Re-spin if needed
steps.detail: If the result comes out crumbly rather than creamy, add a tablespoon of milk and run RE-SPIN. Repeat once if it still needs it.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.detail: Serve topped with a thick berry sauce and chopped dark chocolate.

tips: This makes roughly 7 dl of base, which fills a 710 ml Deluxe pint almost exactly. In a 473 ml pint, make two-thirds of the recipe rather than overfilling — a pint filled past the MAX line spins badly and strains the motor.
Salmiak is ammonium chloride and it is potent. Start at 1 tsp if you have not had salty licorice before; you can always stir more into the second spin.
Xanthan gum clumps instantly in liquid. Whisking it through the dry ingredients first is the whole reason step 1 exists — do not shortcut it.
Freeze the pint standing level. A base that freezes at an angle spins unevenly and comes out crumbly on one side.
16 hours will work in a cold freezer, but a full 24 is noticeably more consistent.

recipes.title: Chocolate Banana Protein Ice Cream
recipes.summary: The reliable one. Ripe banana does most of the sweetening, so the sugar stays low without the flavour going flat.
recipes.imageAlt: A scoop of chocolate banana ice cream topped with whipped cream and crumbled cookies
recipes.article: This is the recipe to start with if you have never made a protein pint before, because banana is extremely forgiving. It brings sweetness, body and just enough starch to soften the chalkiness that protein powder alone gives you, which means the margin for error on everything else is wide. Ripeness is the one variable that matters: a banana with brown spots is significantly sweeter than a yellow one, and if yours is heavily spotted you can cut the sugar to a third of a decilitre without noticing. Cacao powder is bitter and drying on its own, so it needs both the sugar and the mascarpone to land properly. Do not be tempted to skip the cheese.

steps.title: Whisk the dry mix
steps.detail: Whisk all the dry ingredients together until evenly coloured, with the xanthan gum fully dispersed through the powder.

steps.title: Prepare the banana
steps.detail: Break the peeled banana into a few rough chunks and drop it straight into the blender — there is no need to mash it first if you are blending.

steps.title: Blend the base
steps.detail: Add the dry mix and the remaining wet ingredients and blend until completely smooth, about 45 seconds.

steps.title: Fill the pint
steps.detail: Pour into the pint container, stopping at the MAX FILL line.

steps.title: Freeze level
steps.detail: Level the surface, fit the lid, and freeze flat for a full 24 hours.

steps.title: Spin
steps.detail: Spin on LITE ICE CREAM straight from the freezer.

steps.title: Re-spin if needed
steps.detail: If it comes out crumbly, add a tablespoon of milk and run RE-SPIN.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.detail: Serve with whipped cream and crumbled cookies.

tips: This makes roughly 7 dl and is sized for a 710 ml Deluxe pint. Scale to two-thirds for a 473 ml pint.
The riper the banana, the less sugar you need. At heavy brown spotting, 1/3 dl is plenty.
Mashing the banana by hand is only worth doing if you are mixing by hand rather than blending.
Cacao powder and xanthan gum both clump on contact with liquid. The dry whisk in step 1 handles both at once.

recipes.title: Raspberry Lime Sorbet
recipes.summary: Sharp, dairy-free and about six minutes of actual work. Straining the seeds is what makes it feel bought rather than made.
recipes.imageAlt: Deep pink raspberry sorbet scooped into a chilled glass with a lime wedge
recipes.article: Sorbet is where the Creami is at its most convincing, because there is no fat to fake and nothing to hide behind — you are tasting the fruit and the sugar and very little else. That also makes the sugar level non-negotiable in a way it is not with ice cream. Sugar is not only there for sweetness; it lowers the freezing point, and a sorbet made with too little of it freezes into something closer to a solid block than a scoopable pint. If you cut the sugar here, expect to run RE-SPIN twice. Frozen raspberries work exactly as well as fresh and cost a fraction as much, so use whichever you have.

ingredients.metric: 500 g raspberries, fresh or thawed from frozen
ingredients.imperial: 1 lb 2 oz raspberries, fresh or thawed from frozen

steps.title: Make the syrup
steps.detail: Warm the sugar, water and salt in a small pan over a low heat, stirring until the sugar has completely dissolved. Do not let it boil. Set aside to cool to room temperature.

steps.title: Blend the fruit
steps.detail: Blend the raspberries and lime juice until smooth.

steps.title: Strain the seeds
steps.detail: Push the purée through a fine sieve with the back of a spoon and discard the seeds. This takes about two minutes and it is the single biggest difference between a good pint and a gritty one.

steps.title: Combine
steps.detail: Stir the cooled syrup into the strained purée.

steps.title: Fill the pint
steps.detail: Pour into the pint container, stopping at the MAX FILL line.

steps.title: Freeze level
steps.detail: Level the surface, fit the lid, and freeze flat for a full 24 hours.

steps.title: Spin
steps.detail: Spin on SORBET straight from the freezer.

steps.title: Re-spin if needed
steps.detail: If it comes out powdery, add a tablespoon of water and run RE-SPIN.

tips: The syrup must be fully cool before it meets the fruit, or you will cook some of the flavour out of the raspberries.
Do not reduce the sugar. It controls the freezing point, not just the sweetness — less sugar means a harder, more crumbly pint.
Taste before freezing. A sorbet base should taste slightly too sweet and slightly too sharp at room temperature; freezing mutes both.

recipes.title: Mango Passionfruit Sorbet
recipes.summary: Heavy tropical sweetness cut hard by passionfruit acid. No straining needed — the seeds earn their place here.
recipes.imageAlt: Bright orange mango sorbet with passionfruit seeds spooned over the top
recipes.article: Mango on its own makes a sorbet that is pleasant and slightly boring — all sweetness, no edge. Passionfruit fixes that in one step, and the crunch of the seeds gives the pint some texture, which is a rare thing in a sorbet. Ripeness matters more here than in any other recipe on the site. A properly ripe mango gives slightly under thumb pressure at the stem end and smells sweet before you cut it; an underripe one is fibrous, sour, and no amount of sugar will rescue it. If all you can find is hard supermarket mango, leave it on a windowsill for three days rather than pressing on regardless.

steps.title: Make the syrup
steps.detail: Warm the sugar, water and salt over a low heat until the sugar dissolves, then set aside to cool completely.

steps.title: Blend the mango
steps.detail: Blend the mango flesh and lime juice until entirely smooth, with no fibrous threads left.

steps.title: Fold in the passionfruit
steps.detail: Stir in the cooled syrup, then stir in the passionfruit pulp by hand so the seeds stay whole.

steps.title: Fill the pint
steps.detail: Pour into the pint container, stopping at the MAX FILL line.

steps.title: Freeze level
steps.detail: Level the surface, fit the lid, and freeze flat for a full 24 hours.

steps.title: Spin
steps.detail: Spin on SORBET straight from the freezer.

steps.title: Re-spin if needed
steps.detail: If it comes out powdery, add a tablespoon of water and run RE-SPIN.

tips: Blend the mango longer than feels necessary. Mango fibre is the usual reason a tropical sorbet feels stringy.
Add the passionfruit after blending, not before, or the blades will pulverise the seeds and you lose the texture entirely.
Mango varies enormously in sweetness. Taste the purée before adding all the syrup and hold some back if it is already sweet.

recipes.title: Pistachio Gelato
recipes.summary: Dense, savoury-sweet and genuinely green — no colouring, no almond shortcuts, just a lot of pistachio.
recipes.imageAlt: Pale green pistachio gelato in a metal tub with chopped pistachios scattered on top
recipes.article: Most pistachio ice cream is mostly almond extract and green food colouring, which is why real pistachio gelato surprises people the first time — it is duller in colour and far more savoury than expected. The salt is doing real work here, not just seasoning; pistachio is a fatty, faintly grassy nut and without enough salt the whole thing reads as bland. Use unsweetened pistachio butter if you can find it, because the ready-sweetened spreads will push this well past where you want it. If you are grinding your own nuts, expect to run the blender for several minutes and to end up with something closer to a paste than a butter, which is fine.

steps.title: Soften the cream cheese
steps.detail: Beat the cream cheese and sugar together in a bowl until smooth. Doing this first stops the cream cheese seizing into lumps later.

steps.title: Add the pistachio
steps.detail: Add the pistachio butter and salt and beat again until evenly combined.

steps.title: Blend the base
steps.detail: Blend in the milk and cream until the mixture is completely smooth and pale green.

steps.title: Fill the pint
steps.detail: Pour into the pint container, stopping at the MAX FILL line.

steps.title: Freeze level
steps.detail: Level the surface, fit the lid, and freeze flat for a full 24 hours.

steps.title: Spin
steps.detail: Spin on GELATO straight from the freezer.

steps.title: Re-spin if needed
steps.detail: If it comes out crumbly, add a tablespoon of milk and run RE-SPIN.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.detail: Serve with chopped pistachios and a little flaky salt.

tips: Cream cheese straight from the fridge will not incorporate. Leave it out for half an hour first.
Taste the base before freezing and be prepared to add more salt than feels right. Cold blunts salt considerably.
The colour will be dull olive-green, not bright green. That is what pistachio without colouring looks like.

recipes.title: Espresso Stracciatella Gelato
recipes.summary: Bitter espresso base shot through with shards of dark chocolate, added on the mix-in cycle so they stay crisp.
recipes.imageAlt: Coffee-coloured gelato shot through with thin shards of dark chocolate
recipes.article: Stracciatella is not chocolate chip. The difference is that the chocolate goes in as thin, brittle shards rather than solid chunks, so it shatters against the teeth instead of sitting there frozen and waxy. On a Creami you get that by chopping the chocolate very fine and adding it on the MIX-IN cycle at the end, rather than freezing it into the base where the blade would simply grind it away. The espresso should be strong and properly cooled — hot coffee poured into a dairy base will curdle it, and weak coffee disappears entirely once frozen. If you only have instant, use twice as much as the jar suggests.

steps.title: Soften the cream cheese
steps.detail: Beat the cream cheese and sugar together until smooth.

steps.title: Blend the base
steps.detail: Blend in the milk, cream, cooled espresso and salt until completely smooth.

steps.title: Fill the pint
steps.detail: Pour into the pint container, stopping at the MAX FILL line.

steps.title: Freeze level
steps.detail: Level the surface, fit the lid, and freeze flat for a full 24 hours.

steps.title: Spin
steps.detail: Spin on GELATO straight from the freezer.

steps.title: Chop the chocolate
steps.detail: Chop the chocolate as finely as you can manage — you want shards and dust, not chunks.

steps.title: Run the mix-in
steps.detail: Make a well in the middle of the spun gelato, tip in the chocolate, and run MIX-IN.

steps.title: Serve immediately
steps.detail: Serve immediately, while the chocolate is still crisp.

tips: The espresso must be at room temperature or colder before it meets the dairy. Hot coffee will curdle the base.
Chocolate above about 70 percent works best. Milk chocolate goes soft and greasy rather than shattering.
If you skip the mix-in cycle and stir the chocolate in by hand, it will clump. Let the machine do it.
